newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 11.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop said North Korea was fully prepared to launch a war against South Korea and that he was sure the North would attack the South.

- If foreign fishing boats refused to leave Japan's territorial waters despite warnings, it is natural that we should seize them, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said in news conference on Thursday.
- From next month, Korea's large conglomerates will be banned from taking out loans in excess of 45 percent of a single bank's net worth.
- The government, backing away from its hard-line stance, has decided to allow the central bank to exercise full authority on the nation's monetary policies.
- Inter-ministerial conflicts plus U.S. pressure has suspended imports of Russia weapons which were originally brought in instead of the return of loans extended to the former Soviet Union.
- Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha said Japan recently hinted that it would unilaterally scrap the 1965 fishery agreement with Korea unless an agreement is reached on its revision by July 20.
